items.title: Josi lifts Predators past Golden Knights in shootout for seventh straight win
items.summary: Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday night for their seventh straight win.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday night for their seventh straight win. Ryan O’Reilly scored twice for the Predators. Juuse Saros made 40 saves. Victor Olofsson and Rasmus Andersson scored for Vegas, which had its four-game winning streak snapped. Adin Hill stopped 30 shots. Trevor Connelly gave Vegas the early advantage in the shootout, but Filip Forsberg kept Nashville alive with a third-round goal. After Saros denied Jack Eichel, Josi converted to complete the comeback. Braeden Bowman and Mitch Marner also missed for Vegas. Steven Stamkos and O’Reilly were unsuccessful for Nashville. Olofsson nearly ended the game early in overtime, but his shot rang off the post. The Golden Knights extended their point streak to six games despite the loss. Nashville won its fourth consecutive road game. Olofsson continued his productive return from injury with his sixth goal in eight appearances this season. He had a goal and two assists in Wednesday’s 5-3 victory over Utah and entered Friday with four points in three games since returning Nov. 5 at Detroit. Andersson scored his third goal of the season, while O’Reilly increased his total to nine. Nashville entered with strong goaltending throughout its winning streak. Saros and Justus Annunen combined for a 1.63 goals-against average and .942 save percentage over the previous six victories, allowing 10 goals. Saros was named the NHL’s third star of the week Monday after stopping 53 of 55 shots across two wins. The Predators entered the night with the NHL’s second-ranked penalty kill, erasing 89.5 per cent of opponents’ power plays, and stopped Vegas on its only power-play opportunity.

items.summary: This should have been a constructive week for the Vancouver Canucks. A reset. Instead, they returned to regular programming.
items.body: VANCOUVER — This should have been a constructive week for the Vancouver Canucks . A reset. Instead, they returned to regular programming. Staggering through a hectic and historically bad first quarter of the National Hockey League season, the Canucks finally got a chance to rest and practise. But only the resting part was evident Friday against the New York Rangers. The Canucks rested in the second period, surrendering as many goals as they generated shots (four) and were embarrassed again in a 5-1 loss, their 17th defeat in 18 games since Oct. 3 and their eighth straight loss at Rogers Arena. It sounds impossible that in the Year 2026, with the experienced National Hockey League players the Canucks have kept on their roster for the start of the Great Rebuild, the team could be this bad. items.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets have placed winger Conor Garland on injured reserve retroactive to November 6th.
items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Place Conor Garland On IR By Brian La Rose | at November 13, 2026 9:00 pm With the Blue Jackets being a bit banged up with their forward group, they’ve made a roster move to allow them to recall someone if needed. The team announced today that they’ve placed winger Conor Garland on injured reserve. The placement is retroactive to November 6th, meaning that he has already missed the required one week. Accordingly, he can be activated at any time. The team now has one open roster slot. Garland is dealing with an upper-body injury with no firm timeline for his return. The 30-year-old is in his first full season from Columbus after being acquired from Vancouver last season and to say he has struggled would be putting it lightly. Through 15 games, Garland has yet to score while recording one assist. Dating back to last season, he’s on a 29-game goal drought. Still, Garland has a good enough track record to provide some encouragement that he’ll be able to turn things around when he’s cleared to return. While he had a 33-point effort last season, his previous four campaigns ranged between 46 and 52 points. Meanwhile, after leaving last night’s game with an upper-body injury, center Sean Monahan is listed as day-to-day and hasn’t been ruled out of playing on Saturday, notes Aaron Portzline of The Athletic ( Twitter link ). The veteran is also off to a quiet start with one goal and five assists through his 16 appearances. Speculatively, if he isn’t cleared, it wouldn’t be surprising to see Columbus call someone up from AHL Cleveland using the roster slot created with Garland’s IR placement.

items.title: Boeser becomes eighth player to score 500 points with Canucks
items.summary: Brock Boeser has cemented his place in Vancouver Canucks history with a major milestone.
items.body: Brock Boeser has cemented his place in Vancouver Canucks history with a major milestone. The veteran forward collected his 500th point in a Canucks uniform on Friday, becoming just the eighth player in franchise history to do so. Boeser's milestone point came with an assist on a first-period goal by Elias Pettersson. "It means a lot," Boeser told Sportsnet's Dan Murphy during the first intermission. "I've been here a long time and anytime you can get a milestone like that it means the world, and just happy to do it with these guys." The Canucks drafted Boeser in the first round, 23rd overall, of the 2015 NHL Draft, and he is the longest-tenured player on the team. The 29-year-old has skated in 650 games over his 11-year career, collecting 233 goals and 267 assists. The other players to score 500 points with the Canucks are Henrik Sedin (1,070), Daniel Sedin (1,041), Markus Naslund (756), Trevor Linden (733), Stan Smyl (673), Thomas Gradin (550) and Pettersson (529).

items.summary: The Anaheim Ducks have assigned goaltender Laurent Brossoit to AHL San Diego.
items.body: Register Login Ducks Assign Laurent Brossoit To AHL By Brian La Rose | at November 13, 2026 6:59 pm With both regular goaltenders struggling, the Ducks turned to Laurent Brossoit a week and a half ago to try to turn their fortunes around. While he largely did just that, it wasn’t enough to keep his roster spot; the team announced today that the netminder has been sent back to AHL San Diego. The 33-year-old signed a one-year, $1.1MM contract back in the summer and was expected to have a chance to battle for the backup job in training camp. However, Ville Husso won that job and Brossoit cleared waivers in the fall and was assigned to the Gulls. Starter Lukas Dostal has had a rough start to his year, posting a 3.76 GAA and a .866 SV% in his ten starts. Husso checked in at 3.55 and .868, respectively, through his six outings, leading to Brossoit getting a chance. Statistically, he didn’t really fare better, playing to a 3.42 GAA and a .867 SV% in his five outings. That said, the Ducks won four of those five contests, helping to stabilize a disappointing start to the campaign. However, with no appreciable improvement between the pipes despite their recent run, the decision was made to return Brossoit to the minors for now. Brossoit has a 2.56 GAA and a .910 SV% in six games with the Gulls and should return to his starting role with them. Meanwhile, should the goaltending need another short-term shakeup, it wouldn’t be shocking to see Brossoit get at least another short-term stint with the Ducks later on this season. The move gives them a vacancy on their 23-man roster. It also drops them below the cap ceiling (even with having a player on LTIR), per PuckPedia , allowing Anaheim to at least bank a little bit of extra cap flexibility for the time being.

items.body: Coach has Edmonton atop Pacific Division heading into first clash against former team Edmonton Oilers coach Mike Babcock is not getting sentimental over his return to Scotiabank Arena nearly seven years since he was fired by the Toronto Maple Leafs. Babcock will coach against his former team for the first time in Toronto on Saturday (7 p.m. ET; SNO, SNW, SNP, NHLN), when his current team, the Oilers, will go for a fourth straight win. "Yeah, but I mean, this is (seven) years ago; the Beatles broke up, remember," Babcock told reporters while smiling during a press conference after the Oilers practice Friday. The Maple Leafs hired Babcock on May 20, 2015, signing him to an eight-year contract. Toronto finished last in a 30-team NHL with 69 points in 2015-16 and won the 2016 NHL Draft Lottery and the right to select Auston Matthews with the No. 1 pick in the 2016 NHL Draft. From there, the Maple Leafs made the Stanley Cup Playoffs in three consecutive seasons, including setting what at the time was a franchise record with 105 points in 2017-18, but they lost in the first round each time. He was fired on Nov. 20, 2019, just 23 games into the 2019-20 season. "I loved it," Babcock said of his time in Toronto. "I worked with real good people. items.body: Register Login Canucks Activate Filip Chytil; Place Guillaume Brisebois On IR By Brennan McClain | at November 13, 2026 5:30 pm Shortly before their upcoming contest against the New York Rangers, the Vancouver Canucks announced they activated forward Filip Chytil from the injured reserve. In a corresponding roster move, the Canucks placed defenseman Guillaume Brisebois on the injured reserve with an undisclosed ailment. Plagued by concussions throughout his 10-year career, Chytil has recently been dealing with shoulder and upper-body issues. The shoulder ailment delayed his start to the 2026-27 season, and a reaggravation of the injury has caused an additional five-game absence, beginning on October 30th. Because of the injury, Chytil has been limited to two assists in seven games for Vancouver this season. Last year, in another injury-marred season, Chytil finished with three goals in 12 games. Essentially, since the start of the 2025-26 campaign, the former first-round pick has appeared in 19 regular-season contests. Clearly, that’s not the return on investment the Canucks hoped for when they acquired Chytil from the Rangers in the J.T. Miller trade from a few years ago. Still, injuries aren’t new for Chytil, and Vancouver must’ve known about the risks when they acquired him. Meanwhile, Brisebois lands on the injured reserve with an undisclosed injury. The 29-year-old defenseman is one year removed from losing most of his 2025-26 campaign due to multiple injuries and subsequent surgery. He finished the year scoring a goal and an assist in nine games with the AHL’s Abbotsford Canucks. This year, his first in the NHL since the 2024-25 season, Brisebois has registered one assist in six games with a -4 rating, while averaging 15:25 of ice time per game.

items.title: Sudden FAA ground stop throws sports weekend into chaos
items.body: The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground all flights nationwide Friday threw the sports world into chaos, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations, and NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time to travel to their games this weekend. The FAA issued a notice that said the ground stop was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said there was a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centers that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, and that FAA technicians were investigating. “There’s no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying,” Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said. Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left many schools — including No. 2 Utah, eighth-ranked Texas and No. 9 Tennessee — at a standstill as they departed for road games. The Utes play at No. 22 Arizona, the Longhorns visit No. 24 LSU and the Vols are travelling to Texas A&M in three of the bigger games of the weekend. “The Southeastern Conference is aware of the FAA's nationwide ground stop and the potential impact on team travel for this weekend's competitions,” the league said in a statement. “We are in close communication with our member institutions to assess potential disruptions and coordinate appropriate responses. items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid points pace seems to have everyone talking. Including a pair of former Edmonton Oilers who saw Wayne Gretzky's brilliance up close. "The Great One" is the only player in NHL history to eclipse 200 points in a season, doing so four times in a five-year span — last done in 1985-86 — but the Oilers' current superstar is making quite the case to join Gretzky's exclusive group. McDavid entered Friday with 49 points (11 goals, 38 assists) through the first 20 games of the season, putting him on pace to finish the regular season with 206 points — which would surpass Gretzky's 205 (1983-84) for fourth-most in NHL history. And while there's plenty of time between now and the end of the year, McDavid's start has many around the league believing in his chances. "There’s no reason why not. I can’t think of one,” five-time Stanley Cup champ with the Oilers and Hall of Famer Jari Kurri told NHL.com . “He might slow down here and there, but he might come back again. It’s a long season and it’s a lot of games, a lot of travel, but hopefully he stays healthy. “And, sure, if he stays healthy and keeps playing like that, I’m sure he will.” Esa Tikkanen, who also played alongside Gretzky, echoed those sentiments: “When the games come later in the season, they’ll be tougher and it’s going to be harder and harder all the time. I think he has a good chance, but there are still 60 games left. So there’s a long way to go, but if he’s healthy, he can do it.” McDavid's previous highest-scoring season came in 2022-23, when he racked up 153 points (64 goals, 89 assists) through 82 games and took home his third Hart trophy, his fifth of six Art Ross trophies and his lone Maurice Richard trophy. items.title: Report: NHL expected to extend Texas expansion evaluation process
items.body: The NHL doesn't appear ready to finalize expansion plans to Texas just yet. Jennifer Streeter of PuckPedia reports that, according to multiple sources "closely connected to expansion efforts," the NHL is expected to extend the evaluation process to determine whether it will award an expansion franchise to a group led by Texas billionaire Dan Friedkin. The NHL and The Friedkin Group entered a six-month exploratory process in June that was designed to look into the viability of adding a 33rd franchise to Houston or Austin, Texas. That process was due to be completed before the end of the year and an update is expected at the NHL's next Board of Governors meeting in early December. If awarded, the new Texas franchise would come with a $3.5 billion price tag. Of that, $1.5 billion would be earmarked to build a new arena and the other $2 billion paid to the NHL as an expansion fee. Speaking at the last Board of Governors meetings in September, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said the league was in no rush to expand and cautioned that any transaction of this size doesn't happen overnight. “We're not under any time constraint,” Bettman said. “This isn't a situation where we said, 'We're going to expand by X date, get your applications in.’ We're dealing with unsolicited — but we're grateful to have them — expressions of interest. And it'll sort itself out on whatever timetable makes sense to everybody." The NHL has twice expanded in the last decade — to Las Vegas in 2017 and Seattle in 2021 — and now has 32 franchises. The awarding of an expansion franchise requires a three-fourths majority of support in a vote of the league's 32 governors.

items.summary: There will never be another Wayne Gretzky, but, as Mark Spector writes, there’s definitely a Gretzkian vibe around Connor McDavid right now.
items.body: “There was a stat a couple of years ago, where he had less games with no points (12), than he had games with three or more points (13). Like, I don’t get that many points in practice. In a season.” — Oilers defenceman Connor Murphy. TORONTO — There will never be another Wayne Gretzky, hockey’s all-time leading scorer who had more career assists (1,963) than second place Jaromir Jagr has career points (1,921). But as Connor McDavid rolls into Toronto for a Saturday night game against the Toronto Maple Leafs , a 20-game, season-opening points streak in tow, there’s definitely a Gretzkian vibe around McDavid. He is, as Gretzky was, the Toronto-area kid who landed in Alberta’s capital, and the envy of Leafs Nation. And as he readies himself to set a new personal mark by extending his points streak to 21 games on Saturday (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. ABT), like almost any new milestone that McDavid can imagine, it inevitably pales to something Gretzky once did. In this case it was Gretzky’s 51-game points streak in the 1983-84 season in which Gretzky averaged exactly three points per game. That season, Gretzky’s first pointless game came on Jan. 27, at home against New Jersey, his shoulder injured and his spirit waning just five games short of Joe DiMaggio’s iconic 56-game hitting streak in baseball. “We knew he was always going to take care of business, that he was always going to get his chances,” said Paul Coffey, the Evan Bouchard to Gretzky, back in the day. “We never had to say. ‘Okay, let's get Gretz a point tonight.’ Never. But I tell you, if he gives it to you, you’d better (expletive) finish.” Today, the eldest Oiler — 1990-born Mattias Ekholm — came into this world two years after Gretzky’s last Stanley Cup. The Great One never played in the 2000’s.

This season felt like a lost one for the Calgary Flames before it even started, and that wasn't necessarily a bad thing. With multiple key veterans shipped off, a 2026 draft class that featured six players in the first three rounds, and a clear conscious effort from GM Craig Conroy to construct a younger roster, it felt like the only thing the Flames were concerned about was how close they could get to the top of next summer's draft. A five-game losing streak to open up the season while being outscored 27-8 put the Flames on track to live up to the extremely low expectations that were set for them, but they've settled in ever since, and the underlying numbers suggest they could be quite underrated. More Videos For starters, Calgary ranks 10th in the NHL in Corsi For percentage (51.18 CF%) at 5-on-5 according to Natural Stat Trick , which measures the share of shot attempts a team takes and faces. items.body: TORONTO — As teams hit Game 21 of their NHL schedules — a nice, clean quarter-mark divider in an 84-game schedule — we’ve gained real clarity on a number of pre-season questions. I’ve got five thoughts as we hit a schedule milestone, so let’s not waste time: If someone is going to tear down a house and rebuild it, these things are not Step A, then Step B. It’s Step A, and then Steps B all the way through Z. The rebuild takes months, while the teardown takes days. That seems relevant for all the teams that have recently been praised for their savvy teardowns, but watching Chicago stuck in the mud has been a real reminder about the challenge that comes with the other steps. Vancouver is still doing demo work, but San Jose has started to erect walls, and it might not be the mansion they hoped. Detroit appears to be rebuilding using sticks and mud, and it’s not looking great nearly a decade into turning things around. items.title: NHL indicates Finland’s block on Russian athletes could affect future games there
items.body: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press. Finland and Norway both announced plans to refuse entry to Russian athletes Thursday, the same day as the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken played the first of two NHL regular-season games in the Finnish capital, Helsinki. The Finnish restrictions take effect from Monday, after the NHL games, and follow a backlash to Russia being reinstated in the hockey world championships, which is not an NHL event. “We are aware of the government’s position and we’ll have to take that into account," the league said on Friday when asked if the new restrictions would be an obstacle to future games in Finland. The Finnish foreign ministry's statement outlining the restrictions didn't distinguish between Russian athletes on national teams, those competing as neutral athletes, or those on club teams in sports like hockey or soccer. The ministry said Thursday that Russians would only be allowed to work in Finland on “tasks that are essential to Finland’s national interests." It added that Russia “uses sports as a propaganda tool.” The NHL has played regular-season games in Finland as part of its Global Series in 2022 and 2024 and hasn't confirmed any future games there yet. As of the opening day of the 2026-27 season in September, there were 53 Russians on NHL rosters, making up 7.3% of the league. That was the fourth-largest contingent of players from any country. Monahan also sustained a lower-body injury in last Friday’s matchup against the Buffalo Sabres. He missed one day of practice but no game action with that injury. Columbus will hope he can rebound just as quickly from a new, upper-body injury. Monahan has remained an important part of the Blue Jackets lineup. He has recorded six points, 11 shot blocks, and a minus-five through 16 games so far. Monahan’s 53.3 faceoff percentage also ranks third among Blue Jackets centermen, behind Adam Fantilli and Charlie Coyle . The Blue Jackets will face a unique issue if Monahan is forced to miss time. Only three Blue Jackets have taken at least 50 faceoffs this season – their trio of centers, who each have more than 200 so far. Monahan’s absence would likely rotate Cole Sillinger back to the center position. It could also bring center Luca Del Bel Belluz back into the NHL lineup. Del Bel Belluz has appeared in eight games this season, with no scoring. He has 10 points in 38 career appearances in the NHL. Columbus could also tap AHL centers Luca Pinelli or Owen Sillinger . The duo lead the Cleveland Monsters in scoring with 12 and 10 points respectively. How the Blue Jackets decide to approach their replacement could be directly tied to the duration of Monahan’s absence. items.title: Friday Four: How Hurricanes have become a model franchise
items.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes are a well-oiled machine. Michael Amato looks at how they became arguably the best blueprint of how to mould your franchise in the NHL.
items.body: If you ever watch a Carolina Hurricanes game, it looks less like an athletic competition and more like an operation or systematic dismantling of an opponent. The Canes are a well-oiled machine. Each part perfectly connected to the other and everyone pulling on the same rope. Once criticized as a team that couldn’t get over the hump, Carolina is now arguably the best blueprint of how to mould your franchise in the NHL. The Hurricanes' dominance was on full display during last year’s post-season. Carolina didn’t lose a game in the opening two rounds, allowing just 10 goals in a pair of sweeps. They would lose just three games en route to their second Stanley Cup and have picked up right where they left off in this 2026-27 season. The Canes have lost just twice in regulation since October 3rd and are on pace for a 134-point season. In a league powered by elite players, Carolina has done all this without a true superstar or a $10M player. There is such a belief in their system that it feels like they can mould almost any skater into an effective piece of their roster. Where other teams around the league crumble after being hit with adversity, the Hurricanes seem to thrive thanks to some foundational principles. You don’t achieve the consistency the Hurricanes have without utilizing incredible balance up and down your lineup. As mentioned earlier, Carolina doesn’t boast a true superstar. Sebastian Aho , Andrei Svechnikov and Seth Jarvis are great players, but none have the ability to take over a game the way Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Nikita Kucherov or Macklin Celebrini can. The seeds for this season's hot start were planted in the summer after the playmaking centre did some hard rehab to recover from a late-season ankle injury. The injury kept Hage out of the first game of the NCAA championship tournament. items.title: Maple Leafs’ confidence shaken as home slump continues
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs are trying to find their confidence as their losing streak continues.
items.body: TORONTO — As the Toronto Maple Leafs stumble toward the conclusion of what is already the worst six-game homestand in franchise history, Jim Hiller struck a frightening tone. The head coach of this 8-11-2 outfit didn’t point fingers at underachieving offensive stars or struggling defencemen. He didn’t chastise or fume or waste time addressing his frustrated skaters after a fifth consecutive regulation home loss — the worst such stretch for the Leafs since a 1990-91 group that finished dead last in the Campbell Conference. “I see lots of hope. I see it. I see it all over the place. I really do,” Hiller said, following a 5-2 loss to the juggernaut Minnesota Wild. The Maple Leafs have more regulation losses (11) than anyone in their conference. They’ve been outscored 22-9 during a homestand from hell. They can’t play two of their best defencemen because one (Morgan Rielly) is dealing with an injury and the other (Chris Tanev) is susceptible to one . And the vengeful Edmonton Oilers have already loaded their bags into Scotiabank Arena, resting up for a Saturday showdown. Knowing he can’t take a hammer to a team gone fragile, Hiller spoke about the virtues of his bottom-line grinders, who were only on for one goal against versus Minnesota and have provided some noticeable pop during the slump. "So, we talk about hope. Hey, these guys are playing outstanding. If we can bolster them, get a little bit more somewhere else, you know, that’s pretty exciting to have a fourth line like that," Hiller said, dekeing through red flag. "So, there’s optimism, without a doubt. And we'll get there. Doesn't feel like it right now, I know. Feels lousy." The knowing looks may not always extend to Cooley's interviews about reading with his pet rabbit, Tito, doing linear algebra for fun, or reading old books on engineering, but most goalies can relate to his thoughts about playing in the subconscious mind and seeking flow state. To quote Maverick, the fighter pilot played by Tom Cruise, in the 1986 film "Top Gun": "You don't have time to think up there. If you think, you're dead." Stopping pucks in the NHL is not quite as dramatic, but it is a fitting quote for Cooley, who first went viral three seasons ago with the San Jose Sharks for sharing the in-game mantra he used to avoid overthinking: "Nothing matters. Nobody Cares. We're all going to die." The "Top Gun" quote is also one most NHL goalies have long understood. There really is no time to think out there. At least not consciously, which brings us to Cooley's subconscious quote, delivered after a 34-save, 3-2 win against the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 18. "I felt nothing," Cooley told Sportsnet's Brendan Parker. items.body: BOSTON — A win is a win, and the Montreal Canadiens aren’t throwing this one away. Not at TD Garden. Not against these Boston Bruins , who came into the night on a four-game heater and in first place in the Atlantic Division. You must do several things right to open up a 5-0 lead in this building, against this team, at this point, and that’s exactly what the Canadiens did to earn this 5-2 win. But the most important things they should take from it—aside from the two points that put them one ahead of the Bruins and tied with the Tampa Bay Lightning atop the division—are more lessons on how to manage big leads. But hey, it’s mid-November, and if there was ever a time to have some tough ones that still result in victories, it’s now—with plenty of games remaining on the schedule and ample time to refine the process. Games like these help good teams become great. They help them dig into the details, and that’s what the Canadiens need to do to ascend to the next level. items.summary: Scheifele had previously held the team’s franchise records before the old iterations records were consolidated over the summer.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Mark Scheifele is back at the top of the Winnipeg Jets ‘ franchise record books, as with two goals and an assist on in Thursday’s 8-3 blowout over the Dallas Stars , he tied the Jets’ franchise record for points with the team. Scheifele got both of his goals in the second period. The first came just over seven minutes into the frame, as he capped the tying goal to complete the Jets’ rally from down 2-0. He followed that up with another goal with under two minutes left in the period, with him getting the eventual game-winning goal on the power play to take a 4-3 lead. But point 929 came one minute into the third period, as he dished the puck to Gabriel Vilardi from behind the net, who then set up Kyle Connor in the faceoff circle for a sharp-angle shot to make the game 6-3, and begin to put the game out of hand. With the effort, Scheifele ties Dale Hawerchuk for the Jets’ franchise record for points with 929. Hawerchuk did it in quicker fashion, as he needed just 712 games to reach the mark, going pointless in his final game as a Jet before he was traded to the Buffalo Sabres in 1990. However, both players have almost identical stat lines to reach the mark, as Scheifele has 378 goals and 551 assists, while Hawerchuk has 379 goals and 550 assists. Scheifele had actually previously held the franchise record until last summer, as at the time, the Jets’ franchise history consisted only of their time as the Atlanta Thrashers from 1999 to 2011 and the current iteration of the Jets. items.body: DALLAS — Mark Scheifele had two goals and an assist, and Dawson Mercer had his second consecutive two-goal game as the Winnipeg Jets rode a five-goal second period and scored the final six goals to rally past the Dallas Stars 8-3 on Thursday night. Kyle Connor and Gabriel Vilardi had a goal and two assists each, Dylan Samberg had a goal and an assist and Cole Koepke also scored as the Jets won their fifth consecutive game. Stuart Skinner made 30 saves. Arttu Hyry, Roope Hintz and David Perron scored for the Stars. Jake Oettinger, who went in with the NHL’s fourth-best goals-against average at 1.99, allowed a season-high six goals on 27 shots and was pulled a minute into the third period. Casey DeSmith gave up two goals, within 15 seconds, on two shots in the highest-scoring game by a Dallas opponent this season. Perron gave Dallas a 3-2 lead midway through the second period with his first goal since the 38-year-old was signed as a free agent on Oct. 15. A three-goal Jets surge closed the period, beginning with a goal at 13:55 by Mercer, acquired on Oct. 25 from New Jersey in the Connor Hellebuyck trade, and capped by Mercer’s score with 7.3 seconds left. Scheifele has four goals and four assists in the last four games. Each team had a goal disallowed — Winnipeg’s for offside and Dallas’ for a kicking motion. The ruling against the Stars negated an assist that would have been the 1,000th career point for captain Jamie Benn. Winnipeg’s Cole Perfetti and Dallas’ Thomas Harley and Nils Lundkvist had two assists each. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that St. Louis’ Mason McTavish preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to his goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 5:28 (14:32 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Mark Scheifele ties Dale Hawerchuk’s Winnipeg Jets points record
items.summary: Scheifele had two goals and an assist in Thursday’s 8-3 win over the Dallas Stars to tie Dale Hawerchuk for the most points in Winnipeg Jets history.
items.body: Mark Scheifele has officially tied his mentor as the greatest scorer in Winnipeg Jets history. Scheifele had two goals and an assist in Thursday's 8-3 win over the Dallas Stars to tie Dale Hawerchuk for the most points in Winnipeg Jets history. Scheifele now has 929 points, the same total Hawerchuk had with the original Jets. The two goals Thursday gave Scheifele 378 goals in his career, one behind Hawerchuk's 379 for the most in franchise history. The milestone comes after the NHL announced this summer that statistics from Jets 1.0 and 2.0 are now merged, something made possible after the Arizona Coyotes went dormant in 2024. Scheifele was the first-ever draft pick by Jets 2.0 after moving to Winnipeg from Atlanta in 2011. Since then, he has been a consistent offensive star for the Jets over his 14 NHL seasons, including scoring a career-high 103 points last season. This season, he has 22 points in 20 games. Before being drafted by the Jets, Scheifele played under Hawerchuk when the Jets legend coached the OHL's Barrie Colts. The two formed a bond that continued as Scheifele moved to Winnipeg. Hawerchuk played nine of the 16 seasons in his Hall of Fame career with Jets 1.0 from 1981 to 1990. He died of cancer in 2020 at age 57.

items.summary: Anton Lundell scored his second goal of the night with 2:40 left to cap a rally from three goals down, and the Florida Panthers pulled off their biggest comeback of the season to beat the Detroit Red Wings 5-4 on Thursday night.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Anton Lundell scored his second goal of the night with 2:40 left to cap a rally from three goals down, and the Florida Panthers pulled off their biggest comeback of the season to beat the Detroit Red Wings 5-4 on Thursday night. Detroit led 4-1 with less than 30 seconds left in the second period, but from there, it was all Florida. Lars Eller, Gustav Forsling and Sam Reinhart also scored for the Panthers, and Carter Verhaeghe had three assists. Andreas Englund got his first goal in more than two years, Marco Kasper also had his first of the season, and Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher also scored for Detroit. Moritz Seider had two assists, but the Red Wings lost their fifth straight. Reinhart’s goal was 3:52 into the game — his 200th with the Panthers — and gave Florida a 1-0 lead, but Detroit scored the next four. It was only the third instance of a 4-0 run in a game by Detroit this season, and it still wasn't enough. Englund’s third career goal was his first since Oct. 17, 2024, at Montreal — and his other goal, in 2023, was at Toronto. He hadn’t scored in 85 games on U.S. soil before Thursday. Kasper’s goal just past the midpoint of the second period pushed the Detroit lead to 4-1, prompting some boos from an impatient home crowd. Forsling scored with 18 seconds left in the second to get Florida within two, and Lundell connected 2:32 into the third to make it 4-3. Eller tied it with 3:31 remaining and then Lundell got the winner less than a minute later. The Panthers entered Thursday as the only team in the NHL without a point against a divisional opponent yet this season. They're now 1-4-0 in games against Atlantic Division rivals.

items.body: Shane Pinto celebrated his birthday in style Thursday night scoring his second goal of the game 2:08 into overtime to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 4-3 win over the Colorado Avalanche . Tim Stutzle and Drake Batherson also scored for the Senators (12-6-2). Linus Ullmark returned to the lineup for the first time since Oct. 21 and made 26 saves. The Avalanche lost more than the game. Superstars Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar did not finish the game due to lower-body injuries in the second period. MacKinnon left the game with just over eight minutes remaining after taking a check from Artem Zub in the hip area and was seen grabbing his right side. Makar was injured moments earlier. Arturi Lehkonen, Parker Kelly and Gabriel Landeskog scored for the Avalanche (11-6-3). Scott Wedgewood stopped 22 shots. Kelly, who had left the game in the second period, tied the game 2-2 with a short-handed goal at 3:54 of the third. The Senators tied it with 3:56 remaining when Batherson snagged a loose puck in the crease and buried his 10th of the season to send it to overtime. Senators: With Ullmark back in goal, the Senators played with an added level of confidence. Avalanche: Despite falling behind early and losing players to injury, the Avalanche stuck to their game. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Columbus Blue Jackets announced on social media that forward Sean Monahan left Thursday’s game against the Tampa Bay Lightning with an upper-body injury and would not return. It’s not clear how Monahan suffered the injury but he did not join the team on the bench for the third period. He finished the game with one assist in 9:58 of ice time. Monahan, 32, has one goal and six assists for seven points in 17 games with the Blue Jackets in 2026-27. He signed a five-year, $27.5-million contract with Columbus ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. Through 14 NHL seasons, the Brampton, Ont., native has 277 goals and 361 assists for 638 points in 913 career regular-season games with Columbus, the Winnipeg Jets , Montreal Canadians and Calgary Flames . During that time, he’s posted three 30-goal campaigns and four 40-point seasons. He reached career highs in all offensive categories with the Flames in 2018-19 when he finished with 34 goals and 48 assists for 82 points. He’s also scored 10 goals and recorded 12 assists for 22 points in 35 Stanley Cup Playoff appearances. Taken with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2013 NHL Entry Draft, Monahan spent three seasons playing junior hockey in the Ontario Hockey League with the Ottawa 67’s. He scored 84 goals and added 119 assists for 203 points in 185 career regular-season games. He also had 10 goals and nine assists for 19 points in 22 OHL playoff games. The Blue Jackets are now 7-10-0 with 14 points through their first 17 games of 2026-27. items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Vladislav Kolyachonok scored the go-ahead goal early in the third period and Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves as the New Jersey Devils beat the Washington Capitals 5-2 on Thursday night in the first of a two-game set. Kolyachonok’s shot trickled past Capitals goaltender Logan Thompson at 6:27. It was the first game in a Devils uniform for the 25-year-old defenseman, who signed in July as a free agent. He was in the lineup in place of the injured Johnathan Kovacevic. Evan Rodrigues, Lenni Hameenaho, Stefan Noesen and Jack Hughes also scored for the Devils, who have won seven straight home games. Hellebuyck returned to the ice after the Devils held him out of Tuesday's loss at Winnipeg, the team that traded him to New Jersey last month. Hellebuyck was booed by Jets fans and said incidents involving his family had prompted his demand to be traded. He has won his first six starts with New Jersey. The Devils are 12-3-0 in their last 15 games and 9-2-0 overall at Prudential Center. Ryan Leonard and Pierre-Luc Dubois scored for the Capitals, who had their two-game winning streak stopped. Thompson stopped 24 shots. Rodrigues opened the scoring on the power play 2:20 into the first. Leonard tied it on the power play later in the period. Dubois put the Capitals ahead early in the second. Hameenaho knotted the score 2-2 with his first goal this season, deflecting Brendan Dillon's shot past Thompson. Noesen scored at 17:07 of the third, and Hughes had an empty-netter. The Devils, who missed the playoffs last season, are second in the Metropolitan Division with 28 points.

Michael McCarron and Danila Yurov, into an empty net, also scored for Minnesota (14-3-4), which got 26 saves from Jesper Wallstedt. Kirill Kaprizov had three assists. Yurov added an assist for a two-point night. The Maple Leafs (8-11-2) have lost the first of five contests of what has turned into a disastrous six-game homestand to move to an ugly 1-7-0 over their last eight. The Wild improved to 8-0-2 over their last 10 since last losing in regulation to the Calgary Flames on Oct. 22. Fellow blueliner Morgan Rielly (lower body) remains on the club's long list of injured players. Toronto defenceman Darren Raddysh took a penalty midway through the second that led to Boldy tying the game 2-2 on a power play. Quinn Hughes picked up an assist on Boldy's second to give the Minnesota defenceman a point streak of at least 10 games for the third time in his career. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Winnipeg’s Cole Perfetti preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Kyle Connor’s goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 3:32 (16:28 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

When he took the job as coach of the Edmonton Oilers , Mike Babcock knew how high the bar was going to be for him. items.body: VANCOUVER — In a place like this, you wouldn’t think it possible to be a fair-weather player. But it is our most basic human nature to take shelter from the elements, and you’d be surprised how many Vancouver Canuck players over the decades were easy to find after wins, when it was sunny, but impossible to locate when it was raining. Right now, it is absolutely pouring on the Canucks, who reach the one-quarter mark of their rebuild season on Friday carrying not only the worst 20-game record in franchise history (3-16-1) but one of the worst on record with the National Hockey League. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports Showtime is back in action in the Windy City. On Thursday, the Chicago Blackhawks activated forward Patrick Kane from injured reserve. With that, he’s expected to be in the lineup for that night’s game, as the Blackhawks are set to play host to the Buffalo Sabres . Kane’s return seemed imminent, as he has been practicing with the main group for the past couple of days. He has missed the past three games after suffering an upper-body injury last Monday against the Colorado Avalanche . He left the contest, which saw the Hawks lose to the Avs by a final score of 5-2, in the second period. He was later placed on IR . This is the first game Kane was eligible to return to the lineup, as Chicago hasn’t played since suffering a 9-2 drubbing at the hands of the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes last Saturday. With Kane out, Chicago extended its losing streak, which is now up to six games. Kane has been one of the Hawks’ more productive players so far this season, though that isn’t saying much. The 37-year-old has a goal and eight assists for nine points in 15 contests, placing him second on the team in helpers behind Connor Bedard, and third in overall scoring behind Bedard and Roman Kantserov. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Good news in Tinseltown, as a top offensive weapon is set to return to the ice. The Los Angeles Kings announced that forward Kevin Fiala is set to make his 2026-27 season debut on Thursday night, as the Kings host the New York Islanders . Fiala has been out of action since suffering a gruesome leg injury while representing Switzerland at the 2026 Winter Olympics. The injury led him to undergo surgery that knocked him out for the rest of the 2025-26 season. Fiala also missed training camp and the first month of the new campaign while recovering. The 30-year-old will be a welcome addition to the lineup, as the Kings have struggled through the first quarter of the year. Through 16 games, Los Angeles has scored just 45 goals, which ranks 30th in the NHL. They also have a goal differential of -10, tied for 24th in the league. Fiala has been one of the Kings’ top scoring threats since he joined the organization in 2022. After posting consecutive 70-point campaigns, he registered 60 points in 81 games during the 2024-25 season. He was on pace to reach 60 points again last year before the injury, as Fiala had notched 18 goals and 40 points in 56 games prior to the Olympic Break. In 707 regular-season games in the NHL, Fiala has posted 229 goals and 299 assists for 528 points, with another 30 points in 49 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Fiala is in the fifth season of the six-year contract extension, which he signed in June 2022. The deal carries an AAV of $7.875 million and includes a modified no-trade clause. The Kings (5-9-2) have lost back-to-back games heading into Thursday, and sit seventh in the Pacific Division , nine points back of the Utah Mammoth for the last Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

items.body: First-ever Finnish-born goalie to make Hockey Hall of Fame does honors CAR@SEA: Rinne joins Aho and Kakko for the ceremonial puck drop in Finland An adoring crowd in Helsinki welcomed Pekka Rinne with a rousing ovation just before he dropped the ceremonial puck at the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki on Thursday. Rinne, who became the first ever Finnish-born goalie inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame earlier this week, did the honors ahead of the game between the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken. He was inducted to the Hockey Hall on Monday as part of the Class of 2026 alongside NHL players Carey Price , Patrice Bergeron , Keith Tkachuk and women's player Cindy Curley. Longtime executive Brian Burke was inducted as a builder. Rinne, who hails from Kempele, was on hand to do the honors in Helsinki for the special event. Instead of the captains taking the honorary faceoff, a pair of Rinne's Finnish countrymen did the honors: Hurricanes forward Sebastian Aho , from Rauma and Kraken forward Kaapo Kakko , a native of Turku. Rinne played 15 NHL seasons and posted 369 career wins, tied for 22nd most in NHL history. He won the Vezina Trophy 2018 and the King Clancy Trophy in 2021. His 2.43 goals-against average is 20th best in League history and career .917 save percentage is 14th all-time.

Nikita Kucherov recorded a hat trick and Brandon Hagel scored two goals of his own. Sabres goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen gave up five goals on 14 shots, while backup netminder Colten Ellis, who took over the crease less than two minutes into the third period, allowed three goals on just eight shots. On Thursday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss Buffalo’s goaltending woes and what the future holds for a team looking to earn another playoff berth this spring. Tyler Yaremchuk : UPL gets the start and gets yanked early in the third period after giving up five goals on 14 shots. Ellis comes in cold early in the third period … if you’re going to pull UPL, do it after the second period, don’t just do it one minute into the third period. Carter Hutton : It’s a tough spot to be in, but if you’re Ellis, this is what you have to do. When you have a chance to go in, you have to find a way to stop the bleeding. It’s a tough spot, but when you aren’t the guy, you aren’t the guy. In Buffalo, there’s probably a lot of concern with how this team is going. After you break that 14-year playoff drought, and now Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram are gone, you’re wondering what is this team? Are we back in the mix? It’s a tough Atlantic Division . Now, Connor Hellebuyck’s name has swirled around Buffalo since the summer, and all of a sudden, you see him be undefeated for the New Jersey Devils and you’re watching your goalies struggle to make saves. items.title: Former USNTDP stars highlight CHL roster for 2026 showcase against USA
items.summary: Some players familiar with the American program will be representing the CHL next month.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: (Steven Ellis/The Nation Network) Some familiar faces are set to battle in the annual showcase. On Thursday, the Canadian Hockey League released the entire roster set to represent the league in the 2026 CHL USA Prospects Challenge. Among the players added for the event set to take place in Quebec next month are some U.S. National Team Development Program alums, including forward Jamie Glance. Glance was one of the top scorers for the USNTDP last year, scoring 56 points in 62 games with the Under-18 squad, while posting 26 points in 25 games with the team during USHL action. The New Hampshire native added another five points during the 2026 IIHF Under-18 Men’s World Championship, which saw the Americans get shockingly eliminated in the quarterfinals. The Boston University commit made the move to the QMJHL this season and has been fun to watch with the Saint John Sea Dogs. In 18 contests, the 18-year-old has nine goals and 14 assists for 23 points. Glance joins Carter Meyer and Levi Harper, who were previously named to the CHL’s roster, as former USNTDP stars who decided to join the major junior ranks before heading off to college. The trio will go up against some old friends, as the U.S. Under-18 Team looks to pick up their second victory in the showcase’s young history. The full CHL roster features 13 Canadians, four Americans, and three Russians, with defenseman Filip Kovalcik and goaltender Vilmer Salen Forsberg hailing from Slovakia and Sweden, respectively. Half of the 22-player roster won gold for Canada this past August at the Hlinka Gretzky Cup . This will be the third edition of the CHL USA Prospects Challenge. items.title: Zayne Parekh is blossoming into a star with the Calgary Flames
items.summary: Parekh is already the Flames’ most exciting young talent in years, and he’s only getting better.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn ImagesSergei Belski-Imagn Images The Calgary Flames haven’t had a young skater as exciting and talented as Zayne Parekh in a long, long time. items.title: Sedins unhappy with Canucks’ results, weighing options amid dismal season
items.body: Daniel and Henrik Sedin say they're not happy with the Vancouver Canucks ' results, but they believe in their coaching staff and players. The NHL team's co-presidents of hockey operations spoke to reporters on Thursday about the beleaguered club, which sits at the bottom of the league standings with a 3-16-1 record. The Canucks have lost six straight games and 16 of their last 17. Daniel Sedin says they're evaluating players every day but have yet to see the group put together a full, consistent effort over an entire game. His twin brother, Henrik Sedin, says Vancouver's front office is "looking at all players" to see what options are available for improving the team, but that the Canucks won't simply trade top talent away to get more draft picks because they need players who can produce on the ice and support up-and-coming athletes. The Sedins played their entire 17-season NHL careers in Vancouver and were appointed the team's co-presidents of hockey operations in May after the Canucks finished the 2025-26 season last in the league.

items.title: Canadiens’ Mike Matheson returns to lineup after six-game absence
items.summary: Matheson has been out of action due to a lower-body injury, though Montreal remains near the top of the Atlantic.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Some reinforcements are coming back to the Montreal Canadiens ahead of a thrilling matchup. On Thursday, the team announced that defenseman Mike Matheson will be back in the lineup for that night’s game, which will see the Canadiens pay a visit to the rival Boston Bruins. Matheson has been out of action for the past six games due to a lower-body injury, though it remains unclear when he was hurt. His last appearance came on Oct. 27, when he picked up two assists in a 2-0 victory over the St. Louis Blues . With Matheson out of the lineup, the Canadiens have done well, going 4-0-2, though the team lost to the Minnesota Wild in overtime this past Tuesday night. The 32-year-old has struggled to stay in the lineup this season, as he has missed a total of 10 games so far in 2026-27. Another lower-body injury led to him missing time in October as well. In his eight appearances this year, Matheson has scored one goal and three assists for four points, a little bit better than the scoring pace he has had over the past two seasons, which saw him score 31 points and 37 points in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 campaigns, respectively. The Quebec native is in his first season of the six-year contract extension he signed last November, which carries a cap hit of $6 million through the 2030-31 campaign. The Canadiens (11-3-4) are riding an 11-game point streak heading into Thursday night’s action. Montreal sits tied for second in the Atlantic Division with the Tampa Bay Lightning , one point back of the first-place Bruins.

items.title: Oilers quarter-mark report card: Edmonton off to very promising start
items.summary: Twice before, the Oilers have managed only three regulation losses through 20 games — and both seasons ended with a Stanley Cup. Is history bound to repeat itself? Sportsnet’s Mark Spector explores in his quarter-mark report card for the team.
items.body: EDMONTON — The last time the Edmonton Oilers had an opening 20 games like this, they won the Stanley Cup. And the only other time they had only three regulation losses in the first 20 games? You can always find something to complain about — we’re sports writers after all. But a 14-3-3 record and the most points in the entire National Hockey League at the time of this writing isn’t exactly a ham sandwich. Especially considering that Zach Hyman has only played nine of 20 games, while second-line centre Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and third-line pivot Jason Dickinson have each played just 11 games. Winger Matt Savoie has yet to play his first game — that’s an entire second line on the shelf most nights. “With the injuries we’ve had, we've done well. In saying that, we’ve got a long, long way to go,” head coach Mike Babcock said. “Twenty games in is real. You've (reached) a mark, and you've been able to assess what you're doing. items.title: Will Quinn Hughes stay? Analyzing the Wild’s play through 20 games
items.summary: Will he or won’t he? The major storyline around the Minnesota Wild this season is whether or not their star defenceman will sign a new contract. Adam Vingan explores the team’s play through one quarter to examine if they’re standing out as a contender with Hughes.
items.body: The will-he-or-won’t-he drama surrounding Quinn Hughes ’ future with the Minnesota Wild rages on as the superstar defenceman still has not committed to the team past this season. Wild general manager Bill Guerin told reporters Tuesday that the situation is “status quo” and he would be willing to keep an unsigned Hughes past the March 1 trade deadline. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.” There was no word on whether Guerin’s fingernails were chewed down to the skin when he said that, and no one would blame him for being incredibly nervous. Hughes told The Athletic that “this is the best hockey I’ve played,” and his impact on the Wild’s rise is undeniable. Minnesota, which is on a nine-game point streak (7-0-2), is battling for the top spot in the Western Conference at 13-3-4. On Tuesday, Hughes became the second-fastest defenceman in NHL history to reach 80 points with a franchise (68 games). Only Hall of Famer Paul Coffey (53 games with the Pittsburgh Penguins) did it faster. “You don’t want to say you come to expect it,” Wild forward Nick Foligno told reporters . “But you just know there’s brilliance … every time he goes on the ice.” The Wild, to their credit, have put together an impressive sales pitch for Hughes on the ice, starting with their top three forwards. items.body: Register Login East Notes: Matheson, Pesce, Kolyachonok By Marcus Antonelli | at November 12, 2026 11:30 am Mike Matheson is coming back for a big Thursday night tilt, announced by the Canadiens . A major insertion into the lineup for Montreal tonight, Matheson missed the past two weeks with a lower-body injury. The 32-year-old has led the team in ice time every year since the team acquired him back in 2022, and despite the missed time, he’s remained the league leader in shorthanded playing time per game out of the gate, averaging 4:28 of PK TOI in 2026-27. Matheson has tallied four points in eight games thus far in a little under 24 minutes per night of playing time. The Bruins have a record of 7-2-1 and have a goal differential of 8 vs. the Canadiens in their last 10 games against each other. Boston is also a huge challenge for a Montreal team that can surpass them for the top spot in the Atlantic over their historic rivals, especially at TD Garden this season, where the B’s are 8-1-0.
